boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented University of Redlands ceremonies, school-spirit practices, and recurring community events.

cards.title: Hear the Redlands Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: A formal University of Redlands tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the Alma Mater at a formal University occasion, and use the official lyrics to recognize the song without disrupting the program.
cards.short_summary: The University’s Alma Mater is sung at commencements, convocations, and other formal occasions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that its Alma Mater, written in 1914, is sung at commencements, convocations, and other formal occasions.
cards.access_notes: Attendance and guest access depend on the particular formal event.

cards.title: Learn the Och Tamale Chant
cards.subtitle: Redlands football, Homecoming, and alumni tradition
cards.notes: Use the official text to follow the chant at an eligible campus or alumni gathering, and join only when event organizers invite participation.
cards.short_summary: A school-specific cheer used after Bulldog touchdowns and at Homecoming and alumni events.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says Och Tamale is recited when the Bulldogs score a touchdown, at Homecoming and alumni events, and as an alumni greeting.
cards.access_notes: Event schedules and spectator access vary; follow staff direction for participation.

cards.title: Spot the Redlands “R”
cards.subtitle: San Bernardino Mountains landmark and Redlands tradition
cards.notes: View the mountainside “R” from a lawful public vantage point, then use the University history to connect the landmark with its annual upkeep.
cards.short_summary: The large mountainside letter remains a central Redlands symbol and maintenance-trek tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies the Redlands “R” as a major tradition and says alumni, students, employees, and friends make an annual maintenance trek.
cards.access_notes: Do not enter the hillside or join maintenance work without University-organized authorization.

cards.title: Watch for George the Bulldog
cards.subtitle: University of Redlands live-mascot tradition
cards.notes: Check official mascot updates for a scheduled public appearance, and give George and his handlers space while taking photos from an appropriate distance.
cards.short_summary: George is the University’s eighth live Bulldog mascot and continues a tradition dating to 1918.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies George as its eighth Bulldog mascot and describes the Bulldog nickname as an enduring Redlands tradition.
cards.access_notes: Appearance times are scheduled by the University; do not approach or handle the mascot.

cards.title: See the Feast of Lights
cards.subtitle: University of Redlands seasonal worship tradition
cards.notes: Review the official event page for the next presentation and ticket instructions, then attend as a respectful audience member if the service fits your plans.
cards.short_summary: A Redlands worship service combining spoken word, tableaux, song, and instrumental music.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls Feast of Lights one of its recognizable traditions and says it was first presented at Redlands in 1947.
cards.source_title: Feast of Lights | University of Redlands
cards.access_notes: The official event page provides ticket information; dates and availability change by year.

cards.title: Notice the Ceremony of Candles
cards.subtitle: Closing rite of Redlands’ Feast of Lights
cards.notes: If attending Feast of Lights, remain through the closing candle ceremony and follow all venue instructions for seating, photography, and any audience participation.
cards.short_summary: A traditional candle rite that concludes the University’s Feast of Lights service.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that Feast of Lights concludes with the traditional Ceremony of Candles, symbolizing the spreading of Christ’s message.
cards.source_title: Feast of Lights | University of Redlands
cards.access_notes: This is part of Feast of Lights; ticketing and participation guidance are set for each presentation.

cards.title: Mark the year at Convocation
cards.subtitle: New-student welcome ceremony at Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Eligible new students and guests can follow the official orientation guide for procession check-in, line-up instructions, and Memorial Chapel attendance details.
cards.short_summary: The Convocation procession and ceremony formally welcome new students to Redlands.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s orientation guide describes Convocation as its official welcome and includes a procession check-in for students.
cards.access_notes: This is orientation programming; eligibility, date, and guest access are announced for each incoming class.

cards.title: Plan around Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: University-wide Redlands reunion tradition
cards.notes: Use the University’s current Homecoming information to choose an open activity, confirm registration needs, and avoid assuming every listed event is free.
cards.short_summary: A University weekend for reconnecting through athletics, family activities, and alumni gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Homecoming and Family Weekend as a time for alumni, families, and the community, including a football game and family-friendly activities.
cards.access_notes: Specific activities, registration requirements, and admission terms vary by year.

cards.title: Gather for All-School Dinner
cards.subtitle: Homecoming tradition on the University Quad
cards.notes: Check the official Homecoming schedule before attending the Quad dinner, and follow the posted guest, meal, and accessibility arrangements for that year.
cards.short_summary: A named Homecoming gathering that brings the Redlands community together on the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The University lists an All-School Dinner on the Quad among Homecoming and Family Weekend activities.
cards.access_notes: Availability, meal arrangements, and admission requirements are set in the current Homecoming schedule.

cards.title: Cheer the Redlands Regatta
cards.subtitle: Homecoming boat race at Thompson Aquatic Center
cards.notes: Look for the event on the current Homecoming schedule, then watch the handmade-boat race from designated spectator areas and follow aquatic-center rules.
cards.short_summary: A named Homecoming race in which students and alumni paddle handmade boats across the pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s Homecoming schedule describes the Redlands Regatta Boat Race as students and alumni racing handmade boats across the Thompson Aquatic pool.
cards.access_notes: The cited schedule labels the race free with RSVP; confirm the current year’s schedule before attending.

warnings: Event dates, tickets, guest access, and participation rules vary. Historical and ceremonial traditions should be experienced only through currently authorized University programming.
